To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed and validated three lateral flow immunochromotographic assays for the detection of ZEN in cereals.
we have developed three kinds of lateral flow assays for the detection of ZEN in cereals, based on colloidal gold, quantum dot, and polystyrenes as labels.
we have developed a simple and rapid lateral flow immunochromatic assay for the detection of ZEN in food samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid and sensitive method for the determination of ZEN in cereals.
a simple, rapid, sensitive, and cost-effective detection method for ZEN.
the development of three novel ICAs for the determination of ZEN in cereals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the three assays developed in this study are highly suitable for rapid, simple, and sensitive ZEN analysis in cereals.
the three ICAs are rapid, simple, and sensitive methods for the determination of ZEN in cereals.
the use of quantum dots or polystyrene beads as labels in ICAs for ZEN is more advantageous than the use of colloidal gold, as they allow for lower LODs and higher sensitivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of nanopartilces as labels is a good alternative for the detection of ZEN in cereal samples.
the three ICAs can be used to determine the presence of ZEN in cereal samples with good accuracy and precision.
the three assays have similar performance, with the quantum dot based assay being slightly better in terms of LOD and linearity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nanoparticle labels can be successfully applied in ICAs for the detection of ZEN in cereal samples.

lateral flow immunochromoassays based on the use nanoparticle labels can be successfully used to detect ZEN at low concentration in cereals and can be a useful tool for the rapid screening of ZEN in cereals.
nanoparticle labels in lateral flow immunochromatic assays are a promising tool for rapid, simple and cost-effective determination of zearalanone.
